State Law reference— Mobile home location permits, O.C.G.A. § 48-5-492 et seq.
568:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Mobile home means a mobile home or a relocatable home as such terms are defined in O.C.G.A. § 8-2-131; provided, however, that those mobile homes which qualify the taxpayer for homestead exemption under state law shall not be considered mobile homes and subject to the provisions of this article.
(Ord. No. 2012-07, § 1(91-100), 10-8-2012)
569:
(a) Before any person shall locate or relocate a home, building, or mobile home within or out of the limits of the city, he shall apply for and obtain from the city clerk's office or the mayor's designee a permit authorizing the relocation at least two days before movement.
(b) The application shall certify the routing of the movement, date and time of the movement, the tonnage weight of the loaded vehicles moving the home or building, and any and all safety precautions to be utilized in the protection of personal and property rights of others during such movement. The clerk, building inspector or any other person designated by the mayor may require that additional information and/or safety precautions be taken if in his professional judgment the moving plans submitted are not feasible or not all necessary safety precautions are considered.
(c) Upon application, the applicant must disclose the height, width, and length of the building or home to be moved. No permit will be approved without assurance that the move can be made without disturbing or damaging obstructions on the sides or above on the route to be taken. If there are any mailboxes, road signs, overhead wiring, traffic lights/signals, bridges, overhangs, or other obstacles on the route listed in the application, it shall be the duty of the applicant to ensure that the building or home will clear all obstructions without damage.
(d) Upon the submission of a completed application, a permit fee (infra), and approval by the clerk, building inspector, or mayor designee, a permit shall be issued to authorize the movement of such building or home.
(Ord. No. 2012-07, § 1(91-101), 10-8-2012)
570:
It shall be a condition precedent to issuance of any permit required by this article that the applicant of the building, home or mobile home shall submit to the city clerk proof that all city, state and county taxes theretofore accruing and payable with respect to such building, home or mobile home have in fact been paid.
(Ord. No. 2012-07, § 1(91-102), 10-8-2012)
571:
It shall be a condition precedent to issuance of any city permit required by this article that the applicant of the building, home or mobile home shall submit to the city clerk proof that all landowner fees with respect to the movement of such building, home or mobile home have in fact been paid. This is including, but not limited to, permit fees, deposits, bonds, etc., that may be required by the landowner before the home, building, or mobile home may be moved from a lot.
(1) Proof of payment of any landowner fees may be shown by producing the following documents to the city clerk or mayor's designee upon application for a city permit to move such building home, or mobile home:
a. Receipt from landowner evidencing payment of fees; and
b. An affidavit signed and notarized by landowner evidencing all terms and conditions have been met as required by the landowner, including any and all fees.
(2) Should the landowner where the building, home or mobile home sits not require any fees prior to movement, only an affidavit from the landowner attesting that no fees or conditions are required before a building, home, or mobile home may be moved is required to be submitted to the city clerk or mayor's designee upon application for the issuance of a city permit.
(3) Should the landowner be absentee and unable to be located after a reasonable and diligent search, only an affidavit from the applicant is required attesting that the landowner is absentee and that no fees have been required from him.
(4) The same requirements of this section apply shall be adhered to in the cases of the landowner being that of the city. An affidavit and receipt may be obtained from the city clerk's office at the time of application upon posting a bond in the amount established by the city and amendable by resolution. Said bond is collected to ensure the proper cleanup is performed after the movement of any building, home or mobile home off city property and to protect the city from any damages resulting from such move. The city shall return the bond within 14 days of the move upon inspection that the move of the building, home or mobile home was completed without harm to any city property. Otherwise, the bond will be forfeited.
(Ord. No. 2012-07, § 1(91-103), 10-8-2012)
572:
(a) Any owner of a building, home or mobile home who has made application for the location or relocation of such building, home or mobile home, and whose application meets the qualifications of this article, shall be issued a permit and shall likewise be issued a decal.
(b) The applicant shall pay a nonrefundable fee in the amount established by the city and amendable by resolution upon application and upon meeting all requirements pursuant to this article. Thereafter, a permit will be issued authorizing movement of the building, home or mobile home within or out of the city limits. The permit shall accompany the building, home, or mobile at all times of transport within the confines of the city in such a manner as to cause the permit to be easily visible for inspection.
(c) Movement and relocation shall only occur between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. on weekdays, excluding holidays. These times will be subject to change based on availability of escort personnel.
(Ord. No. 2012-07, § 1(91-104), 10-8-2012)
573:
Whenever a permit authorizing the relocation of a building, home or mobile home is issued, and such building, home or mobile home is to be relocated within the confines of the city, a new application shall be made for a move-in permit at the same time a permit is issued pursuant to this article.
(Ord. No. 2012-07, § 1(91-105), 10-8-2012)
574:
The issuance of any permit under the provisions of this article shall in no way be construed as superseding the requirement for the location of mobile homes, as such requirements may be contained within appropriate zoning resolutions or other actions of the mayor and council; and the issuance of a permit under the provisions of this article shall not prohibit the mayor and council from requiring a relocation of the mobile home to a place where such mobile home is permitted by city zoning regulations; but in such case, the owner of such mobile home shall apply for and obtain a permit for each move.
(Ord. No. 2012-07, § 1(91-106), 10-8-2012)
577:
(a) Neighborhoods are facing significant threat of becoming blighted through the lack of adequate maintenance and security of properties that are abandoned, foreclosed or where ownership has been transferred after foreclosure. Improperly maintained and secured abandoned and/or foreclosed properties can become a hazard to the health and safety of persons who may come on or near the property and can adversely affect the aesthetic and economic attributes of communities. Difficulties also often arise in locating the person responsible for the condition of abandoned and/or foreclosed real property. There is a substantial need directly related to the public health, safety and welfare to comprehensively address these concerns through the adoption of the provisions in this article.
(b) The foreclosure registry will require creditors or mortgagees to provide the city with official information for contacting a party responsible for bringing abandoned and/or foreclosed real property into compliance with applicable provisions of article XIII of this chapter; chapter 16, environmental and natural resources; chapter 22, health and sanitation; chapter 36, streets, sidewalks and other public places of the Code for the city.
(Ord. No. 2013-04, § 1(18-400), 8-12-2013)
578:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Abandoned means a property that is vacant and is under a notice of default and/or notice of trustee's sale, pending tax commissioner lien sale and/or properties that have been subject of a previous foreclosure sale in which title was retained by the beneficiary of a deed of trust involved in the foreclosure and any properties transferred under a deed in lieu of foreclosure and/or sale.
Agent means an individual with a place of business in this state at which he is authorized to accept inquiries, notices, and service of process on behalf of a vacant or foreclosed real property owner.
Foreclosed real property means real property that is subject to any process under O.C.G.A. title 44 whereby a grantor of a secured debt in real property is divested of all rights to said real property and title to the real property is not sold in an arms-length transaction but retained by a creditor or mortgagee after a foreclosure sale or proceeding or transferred to a creditor or mortgagee pursuant to a deed in lieu for foreclosure.
Owner means any person or persons having any individual, joint or common title or interest in real property defined by the laws of the state as a legal or equitable estate or interest. If property is owned by a corporation, the owner listed shall also include the registered agent and director/president/CEO of such corporation.
Registration means the filing of a registration statement with the office of code enforcement.
Registration statement means the forms required to be filed with the office of code enforcement pursuant to this article.
Registry means the official record, electronic or otherwise, of registration of structures required by this article.
Street address means the street or route address. The term "street address" shall not mean or include a post office box.
Vacant real property means real property, commercial or residential, that is either:
(1) Intended for habitation, has not been lawfully inhabited for at least 60 days, and has no evidence of utility usage within the past 60 days; or
(2) A vacant lot bearing no structure or a partially constructed or incomplete structure without a valid building permit. Such term shall not include a building or structure containing multiple units with common ownership that has at least one unit occupied with evidence of utility usage.
(Ord. No. 2013-04, § 1(18-401), 8-12-2013)
579:
(a) Duty to register. It shall be the affirmative duty of each owner of real property to file a complete registration statement with the office of code enforcement after 90 days of such property becoming vacant real property within the meaning of this article.
(b) Vacant or foreclosed real property. Registration shall not be required for vacant or foreclosed real property pursuant to this section within 90 days of such real property's transfer:
(1) Where there is a deed under power of sale or deed in lieu of foreclosure; or
(2) To the first subsequent transferee after the vacant real property has been acquired by foreclosure under power of sale pursuant to O.C.GA. § 44-14-160 or acquired pursuant to a deed in lieu of foreclosure.
(c) Penalties for failure to register or to update. Any owner that fails to register or to update the information specified herein shall be in violation of this article and shall be guilty of an offense.
(Ord. No. 2013-04, § 1(18-402), 8-12-2013)
580:
(a) Preparation of registry forms; required information to be filed. Until such time as the state department of community affairs promulgates a standard registry form, the office of code enforcement is authorized to prepare registry forms, in paper or electronic format. On such form, each registrant shall be required to file with the office of code enforcement only the following information:
(1) The real property owner's name, the street address, mailing address, telephone number, facsimile number, and e-mail address;
(2) The agent's name, street address, mailing address, telephone number, facsimile number, and e-mail address;
(3) The real property's street address and tax parcel number;
(4) The transfer date of the instrument conveying the real property to the owner; and
(5) At such time as it becomes available, recording information, including deed book and page numbers, of the instrument conveying the real property to the owner.
(b) Updating information. The owner shall notify the office of code enforcement, within 30 days, of any change in the information provided in the registration statement and regardless of whether the information provided was in the deed under power of sale or deed in lieu of foreclosure, by filing an updated registration statement on a form provided by the office of code enforcement for such purposes. There shall be no fee for the filing of an updated registration statement.
(c) Initial validity/renewal. The registration shall remain valid for 12 months from the date of the filing of the registration statement. In the event that ownership of a registered structure changes during this period, the new owner shall file an amended registration statement within 20 days of accepting the vesting instrument. The owner shall be required to renew the registration for successive 12-month periods as long as the real property remains vacant for any part thereof.
(d) Foreclosed real property not required to register. The office of code enforcement shall not require the transferee/owner/agent of a foreclosed real property to register such property pursuant to this section nor require the payment of any registration fees pursuant to section 10-1010 when any real property is acquired by foreclosure under power of sale pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 44-14-160 or acquired pursuant to a deed in lieu of foreclosure, and:
(1) The deed under power of sale or deed in lieu of foreclosure contains the information specified in subsections (a)(1) through (5) of this section;
(2) The deed is filed with the clerk of superior court within 60 days of the foreclosure sale or transfer of the deed in lieu of foreclosure; and
(3) Proof of the following is provided to the office or officer in charge of the county or municipal foreclosed real property registry:
a. A filing date stamp or a receipt showing payment of the applicable filing fees; and
b. The entire deed under power of sale or entire deed in lieu of foreclosure.
(Ord. No. 2013-04, § 1(18-403), 8-12-2013)
581:
(a) At the time of the filing of the registration statement, the owner shall pay a registration fee in the amount established by the city and amendable by resolution for each vacant real property.
(b) No registration statement shall be deemed filed unless the fee has been paid. For a parcel of land containing two or more buildings under common ownership, only one registration statement and one fee shall be required.
(Ord. No. 2013-04, § 1(18-404), 8-12-2013)
582:
The office of code enforcement is authorized to administer, or contract for the administration of, the provisions of this article pursuant to an electronic and/or web-based registry system for the registration of structures subject to this article.
(Ord. No. 2013-04, § 1(18-405), 8-12-2013)
583:
The owner of any vacant building or dwelling, shall, within 30 days of registration, do the following:
(1) Enclose and secure the building or dwelling;
(2) Post a sign affixed to the building or dwelling indicating the name, address and telephone number of the owner and the owner's authorized agent for the purpose of notice and/or service of process. The name, address and telephone number of a person responsible for day-to-day supervision and management of the building or dwelling, if such person is different from the owner holding title or authorized agent shall be indicated on the sign as well. The sign shall be of a size and placed in such a location so as to be legible from the nearest public street or sidewalk, whichever is nearer; and
(3) Maintain the building or dwelling in a secure and closed condition and maintain the sign until the building or dwelling is again occupied or demolished or until repair or completion of the building or dwelling has been undertaken.
(Ord. No. 2013-04, § 1(18-406), 8-12-2013)
584:
A vacant real property owner, or the agent of such owner, may apply to remove such vacant real property from the registry at such time as the real property no longer constitutes vacant real property. Application for removal from the registry shall be accompanied by corroborating documentation that the real property no longer constitutes vacant real property. Corroborating documentation need not include the names or other personal information of any tenants. The office of code enforcement shall grant or deny such application within 30 days and in the case of denial shall provide notice to the property owner. If the office of code enforcement does not grant or deny the application for removal from the registry within 30 days, the application shall be deemed granted.
(Ord. No. 2013-04, § 1(18-407), 8-12-2013)
585:
(a) Any vacant or foreclosed real property owner affected by this article requiring vacant or foreclosed real property registration may challenge any determination made pursuant to this article. Such appeal shall be made to the city municipal court, filed with the clerk of court within ten days of the decision of the office of code enforcement and shall include:
(1) The property address and/or parcel identification number;
(2) The owner's name and contact information;
(3) The decision from which the owner is appealing; and
(4) The remedy sought.
(b) Upon receiving the owner's appeal, the court shall schedule a hearing on the next available code enforcement court date and provide notice to the owner and/or person filing such appeal by first class mail to the address provided on the appeal.
(c) The court shall also notify the office of code enforcement of such appeal and require the office's presence at such hearing.
(d) After a hearing, the court shall issue a decision and said decision shall be appealable to the county superior court within 30 days by way of writ of certiorari pursuant to O.C.G.A. title 5.
(e) Failure of the owner to appear at such hearing shall the render the decision of the office of code enforcement final.
(Ord. No. 2013-04, § 1(18-408), 8-12-2013)
588:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Corner lot means a lot which has frontage at two intersecting streets.
Fence means any structure erected to provide a barrier, either physical or visual, for the purpose of delineating property lines, protecting property, providing for security and privacy, and/or a means to contain activities on the property.
Fence height means the vertical dimension from the natural ground level to the top of the fence, measured at any point along the length of the fence.
(Ord. No. 2017-11, § 1(62-250), 8-21-2017)
589:
(a) All fences erected after the enacting of the ordinance from which this article is derived must be reviewed and approved by the city engineer prior to construction.
(b) No fence shall encroach into a public right-of-way.
(c) No fence shall be installed so that, in the opinion of the city engineer or chief of police, it prevents or unduly restricts access to a property for emergency purposes.
(d) No fence shall be installed so that, in the opinion of the city engineer or the chief of police, it obstructs, hinders or impedes the movement of the pedestrian or vehicular traffic.
(e) No fence shall encroach into an undisturbed buffer.
(f) Any fence proposed for placement within an easement must be accompanied by documented permission from the titled owner, if applicable, and must be approved by the city engineer.
(g) Structural supports are allowed only within the interior of the fenced yard.
(h) Fences located on nonresidential property shall have the following restrictions:
(1) Maximum height of eight feet;
(2) Allowed only in the side and rear yard areas; and
(3) No fence shall be allowed in a front yard.
(i) Fences located on residential property shall have the following restrictions:
(1) Front yard:
a. Maximum height of four feet;
b. Ornamental in design and limited to brick, masonry, picket or split rail; and
c. Chain link or any other type wire fence shall be prohibited in the front yard.
(2) Side and rear yards: Maximum height of six feet.
(j) Corner lots are considered to have two front yards; therefore, front yard restrictions apply to yard areas adjacent to both streets.
(k) Fences may be located on the property line with a written agreement between the two adjoining property owners which would allow for the connection of two fences (Option "A"). In the event the adjoining property owners do not allow for the connection, it is required that each fence be placed a minimum of three feet inside the property line, leaving a six-foot separation for maintenance (Option "B"). See diagram.
(Ord. No. 2017-11, § 1(62-251), 8-21-2017)
590:
It is the responsibility of the owner of the property on which a fence is located to maintain the fence in a nondamaged, clean, good and proper condition at all times.
(Ord. No. 2017-11, § 1(62-252), 8-21-2017)
591:
Damaged or illegal fences shall be immediately repaired, replaced or removed by the owner, agent, tenant, or person having the beneficial use of the building or structure upon which said fence or wall shall be found. Upon identification of a damaged or illegal fence, the code enforcement officer shall order the property owner via notice of violation to remove or make repairs within ten business days. If the damaged fence is not removed or repaired as ordered within ten business days, the code enforcement officer shall issue a citation to be adjudicated in the city municipal court. After an adjudication of said citation in the court with a finding of guilt, or plea of guilty or nolo contendere, the court shall require the removal or repair within 45 calendar days of plea or finding of guilt. Failure to remedy the fence violation within 45 days shall result in the authority of the city to pursue court approval for the removal or repair at the expense of the property owner. All expenses related to the removal or repair shall result in a lien against the property to which the fence is associated unless reimbursed to the city within ten days of city's removal or repair.
(Ord. No. 2017-11, § 1(62-253), 8-21-2017)
595:
Footnote 1:
State Law reference— Pawnbrokers, O.C.G.A. § 44-12-130 et seq.; local regulation of pawnbrokers, O.C.G.A. §§ 44-12-135, 44-12-136; dealers in precious metals and gems, O.C.G.A. § 43-37-1 et seq.; local regulation of dealers in precious metals and gems, O.C.G.A. § 43-37-5.
596:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Antique dealer means any person who engages in the business or occupation which derives 75 percent of its gross receipts by the selling, bartering or exchanging of any painting, or furniture, china or other object painted or made more than 50 years prior to the date of sale, which is valuable primarily by reasons of age, scarcity, or the skill and craftsmanship of the artist or artisan.
Dealer in precious metals and gems means a person, whether known as a redemption center, gold and silver dealer, pawnshop, or any other name, either owner or manager, whose business involves receiving by buying or trading of, for, or in precious metals such as gold or silver or platinum, including coins and the receiving by buying or trading jewelry, gems or precious or semiprecious stones; however, it shall not include purchases from licensed wholesalers in the normal course of business, nor shall it include pawnbrokers who only take precious metals or gems on pawn or pledge.
Employee means any person employed or allowed to perform duties, whether or not such person receives a salary, wages or other compensation or consideration, but not including the person covered on the license or renewal application.
Flea market means any business which derives 25 percent or more of its gross receipts from the sale, trade or barter of used or previously owned personal property, other than operable motor vehicles, or used major office or major household furniture or major appliances, or used merchandise purchased by lot from bankruptcy sales, estate liquidation sales, and wholesale and retail liquidation sales from licensed dealers.
Flea market operator means any person who leases or rents premises or space to three or more flea market vendors or three or more individuals for the operation of a flea market at any one location.
Flea market vendor means any person who rents or leases space from a flea market operator on a permanent basis or for a period of more than 30 days, for the purpose of selling or offering for sale goods which constituted the operation of a flea market.
Goods carries its normal meaning, should be construed in the broadest sense allowable, and includes all forms of personal property.
Itinerant dealer means any person who is engaged in any temporary or transient business conducted in a shop, room, site or other business rented for any duration less than 30 consecutive days or used on a temporary basis. The term "itinerant dealer" includes, but is not limited to, persons selling handmade items, arts and crafts, salvaged goods, and used household accessories. Any person who is either a pawnbroker, flea market vendor or dealer in precious metals or gems shall not be eligible to be licensed as an itinerant dealer but shall pay the fee and abide by the regulations imposed upon either pawnbrokers, flea market vendors or dealers in precious metals and gems, as the case may be.
Owner means any person owning 25 percent or more of a business.
Pawnbroker means any person who shall in any manner lend or advance money or other things for profit on the pledge or possession of personal property, or other valuable things other than securities or written evidences of indebtedness or who deals in the purchasing of personal property or other valuable things on condition of selling the same back to the seller at a stipulated price.
(Ord. No. 2007-01, § 1(22-161), 4-10-2007)
597:
This article is to be construed as consistent with state law. However, these provisions are to be applied in lieu of state law and state fee and registration requirements whenever possible. It is the intent of the mayor and council that all duties delegated to the chief law enforcement officer of the city and/or that officer's designee shall be exercised as provided in this article.
(Ord. No. 2007-01, § 1(22-162), 4-10-2007)
598:
Businesses which limit the purchase of used valuables to the acceptance of trade-ins for credit for new goods or the dispensing of refunds in regard to valuables previously purchased from such business shall not be regulated or covered under this article.
(Ord. No. 2007-01, § 1(22-163), 4-10-2007)
599:
Each person authorized or allowed to conduct any phase of business covered under this article shall be considered an employee and must have an approved employee permit, and this permit must be displayed along with the business license in accordance with license display requirements.
(Ord. No. 2007-01, § 1(22-164), 4-10-2007)
600:
No license or employee permit shall be issued to or renewed for any person who conducts or is employed in a business in which such owner or employee has, within five years of issuance or renewal, been convicted of, or pled guilty or nolo contendere to, any felony involving any federal or state offense or any federal or state misdemeanor involving theft-related offenses. The licensee will submit the identity of all owners and employees to the business license section on a continuing basis as changes occur. This information is to be forwarded to a law enforcement agency designated by the mayor and council for the purpose of allowing a complete check in order that these character qualifications be fulfilled, prior to the issuance of or renewal of any license or permit issued under this article.
(Ord. No. 2007-01, § 1(22-165), 4-10-2007)
601:
All businesses licensed under this article shall be located in strict compliance with the city's zoning ordinance and at a location with an identifiable street address, which shall be stated on the license or renewal application along with other required information. No business licensed under this article shall change its address to another address within the city without giving advance notice to the city clerk, and receiving of an approval of the change, such approval being granted if the new location complies with this article and the city's zoning ordinance. No business licensed under this article shall be operated in or from a motel or hotel, or other such place of temporary lodging.
(Ord. No. 2007-01, § 1(22-166), 4-10-2007)
602:
All pawnbrokers and dealers in precious metals and gems, and flea market operators shall, in addition to other records, keep books wherein shall be entered an accurate description of all property received by or pledged or sold to them. Such description shall include the brand name of the article, any identifying mark, number, initial, Social Security number or name of any person or company, and a statement of the kind of material of which it is made. In such books there shall be entered also the name, age, address, signature and identification number from a driver's license or similar identification of the person by whom same was delivered, deposited or sold, the name of the broker, agent or employee receiving the item, the time when such transaction occurred, the price paid for the goods purchased and the check number issued if applicable. These entries shall be made no later than one hour after the transaction. A permanent, bound set of the pawn tickets shall constitute the book required by this article. All books and records required by this article and articles pledged or sold hereunder shall at all times be subject to inspection and examination by any law enforcement officer of the city, or any other official designated by the city to inspect such documents, any incorporated municipality or the state. Any person engaged in any business licensed under this article who shall fail or refuse to keep the records as provided in this article, or who shall make false entries concerning the transaction, or who shall fail or refuse to permit an inspection by any law enforcement officer of the city, or other designee of the city, any incorporated municipality or the state of such records and of the property pledged with or sold to them shall be guilty of a violation of this article.
(Ord. No. 2007-01, § 1(22-167), 4-10-2007)
603:
All business licensed under this article, except flea market operators and itinerant dealers, shall use a standard form for pawn and a standard form for purchase; and no ticket may be used for a dual purpose. Standard forms may differ only by the name of the business and business address. The design of this form shall be provided by the city, and the forms shall be numbered and chronologically used and sent to the city's law enforcement or designee. Each number missing from the chronological sequence shall be considered a separate violation of this article.
(Ord. No. 2007-01, § 1(22-168), 4-10-2007)
605:
All businesses licensed under this article shall, when receiving in pawn or in purchasing goods, require a proper identification, driver's license or military I.D. card or state-approved I.D. card or company employee I.D. card containing a picture showing positive identification of the person who is pawning, selling or bartering, and shall verify the identification.
(Ord. No. 2007-01, § 1(22-170), 4-10-2007)
606:
All businesses licensed under this article, except flea market operators and itinerant dealers, shall require every person from whom it accepts goods on pawn or purchase to place the fingerprint of his right index finger (if right index finger is missing, the next finger in line will be used) in ink on the front of the copy of the pawn or purchase ticket, which print is to be sent to the city law enforcement or designee.
(Ord. No. 2007-01, § 1(22-171), 4-10-2007)
607:
Every business licensed under this article shall hold, on the premises designated in the license for doing business, every item required to be listed under section 12-25 for at least 15 days before disposing of same by sale, transfer or shipment. The provisions of this section shall not apply to purchases from licensed wholesalers in the normal course of business.
(Ord. No. 2007-01, § 1(22-172), 4-10-2007)
608:
Every business licensed under this article which takes goods on pawn shall hold such goods for at least 30 days unless redeemed by the owner or on authority of the owner before disposing of same by sale, transfer, shipment or otherwise.
(Ord. No. 2007-01, § 1(22-173), 4-10-2007)
609:
For a period of 15 days from the date of purchase and 30 days from the date of pledge (unless redeemed by or by authority of the person who pledged the goods and excepting itinerant dealers therefrom) all goods purchased or pawned and required to be listed under section 12-25 shall be kept on the premises designated in the license for doing business. Every item required to be kept on the premises under this article shall have attached to it either a copy of the form required in section 12-26 or the number of such form. Any person desiring to examine any merchandise shall first obtain a copy of a police department incident or stolen property report. Upon presentation of a copy of such report to any licensed dealer or employee and upon giving in writing to such dealer a full description of the stolen items sought, including all identifying characteristics, his name, address, signature, identification, and incident or stolen property report number and issuing department, such individual shall be allowed to examine any merchandise, of the type described on the premises. Such written information shall be kept in sequential, dated order in a permanent file or book. This record shall be kept in addition to all other records required in this article.
(Ord. No. 2007-01, § 1(22-174), 4-10-2007)
610:
Any item required to be kept or displayed under the provisions of sections 12-30 through 12-32 shall be so kept in its original form as it existed when first purchased; and its physical characteristics shall not be altered in any material or immaterial manner.
(Ord. No. 2007-01, § 1(22-175), 4-10-2007)
611:
No person licensed under this article shall erase, obliterate, type over, write over or any way cause the original entry on the records required under this article to become illegible. All pawn or purchase tickets filled out in error shall be sent to the city's police department or the city's designee in their numbered order along with daily reports and shall have the word "VOID" typed or written across the front, but such entry shall not be used to cause the original entry to be illegible. If an error is made and the ticket is still to be used, then a single line shall be drawn through the incorrect entry. This line shall not cause the original entry to be illegible, and the correct information entry shall be made on the next available area.
(Ord. No. 2007-01, § 1(22-176), 4-10-2007)
612:
The record of each pawn or purchase transaction regulated by this article shall be maintained for a period of not less than four years from date of transaction.
(Ord. No. 2007-01, § 1(22-177), 4-10-2007)
613:
All businesses licensed under this article shall close their establishment and cease transacting any business no later than 10:00 p.m. each day and begin their operation and commence transacting business at no time before 7:00 a.m. each day.
(Ord. No. 2007-01, § 1(22-178), 4-10-2007)
614:
It shall be unlawful for any person licensed under this article to receive in pawn or in purchase any goods of any character or of any description from any person who has not attained the age of 18 years.
(Ord. No. 2007-01, § 1(22-179), 4-10-2007)
615:
No business transactions by any business licensed under this article shall be conducted outside the building designated as the normal place to conduct transactions unless such business does not have a building. The term "business transaction" means any part of business, including inspection or appraisal of any goods when it is possible for such goods to be taken inside the building where transactions normally are made (the term "possible" being here used in the broadest sense). No person other than those possessing a licensee or employee permit shall be allowed to conduct any form of business transactions or to agree to perform such transactions either inside the establishment or on any part of outside land area covered under address of the license.
(Ord. No. 2007-01, § 1(22-180), 4-10-2007)
616:
No business licensed under this article shall accept any articles which have had the serial number altered, obliterated or removed from such article or which the person who is making the business transaction knows should have a serial number upon it unless such person immediately notifies the city's law enforcement or designee.
(Ord. No. 2007-01, § 1(22-181), 4-10-2007)
617:
No business licensed under this article shall take any item in pawn or purchase, taking full or possession title thereto, without entering each transaction of such goods on his books and on the standard forms as provided in sections 12-25 and 12-26.
(Ord. No. 2007-01, § 1(22-182), 4-10-2007)
619:
As a condition of the granting of the license under this article, every licensee agrees to allow any duly authorized law enforcement officer, pursuant to his official duties, to be and remain on or about his premises without the formality of a warrant, provided such officer does not unduly interfere in the licensee's operation.
(Ord. No. 2007-01, § 1(22-184), 4-10-2007)
620:
It shall be unlawful for any person licensed under this article to purchase precious metals in a melted, smelted or nonformed state unless the purchase is from a registered dealer in precious metals.
(Ord. No. 2007-01, § 1(22-185), 4-10-2007)
621:
Every person licensed under this article shall, immediately upon request, turn over to the city's police department or other designee every item believed by the police department or designee to be a stolen item. The police department shall furnish a property receipt, including a case number of recovery, to the dealer surrendering such items. The item shall be returned to the licensee only after it has been determined that such item is not stolen. If it is determined that such item is stolen, it shall be returned to its lawful owner. The term "police department" as used herein shall mean the city's law enforcement officers or the city's designee to perform such duties.
(Ord. No. 2007-01, § 1(22-186), 4-10-2007)
622:
No business licensed under this article shall be designed or operated so as to allow access to such business immediately from any other business without first exiting the other business into a common or open area to which the public at-large has access.
(Ord. No. 2007-01, § 1(22-187), 4-10-2007)
623:
The mayor and council shall not issue more than one pawn broker, as defined herein, business license per 1,000 acres of area or part thereof for a maximum of two pawnbroker licenses to be issued within the corporate limits of the city.
(Ord. No. 2013-03, § 1(22-188), 3-11-2013)
624:
Footnote 1:
State Law reference— Emergency management, O.C.G.A. § 38-3-1 et seq.
628:
The purpose of this article is to regulate the installation and use of alarm systems, to establish standards for, controls of, and maintenance of the various alarm systems that are intended to bring about police department, fire department and/or other emergency department response, and to provide for user fees and penalties for violations.
(Ord. of 10-15-2002, § 7(54-51))
629:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Alarm system means an assembly of equipment and devices designated and arranged to detect and signal an unauthorized intrusion into the premises, to signal an attempted burglary, robbery or other criminal activity in or upon the premises, to signal a fire in or upon the premises, a medical emergency needing medical attention, and/or an ambulance, or like occurrences.
Enforcement authority means the city or its designee, including the county or one of its departments, including, but not limited to, the county communications department, fire department, and police department.
Owner means the owner, lessee or occupant of the premises having an alarm system regulated under the provisions of this article. The term "owner" means, as well, the person who has control of the premises on which any alarm system which is regulated under the provisions of this article is in operation.
Permitting authority means the city or its designee, including the county department of community development.
Unauthorized alarm means the activation of an alarm system signal resulting in a response by the police, fire or other city or county emergency department where none of the events or emergencies for which the alarm system has been installed have, in fact, occurred.
(Ord. of 10-15-2002, § 8(54-52))
630:
The provisions of this article shall apply to the installation, alteration, equipment, use and maintenance of alarm systems installed within the jurisdiction of the city, after adoption of this section.
(Ord. of 10-15-2002, § 8(54-53))
631:
The provisions of this article shall not apply to the following:
(1) An alarm system installed in a motor vehicle; or
(2) An alarm system installed upon the premises of a federal, state, county or municipal government, or body politic of such governments, or the county school system.
(Ord. of 10-15-2002, § 9(54-54))
632:
Nothing contained in this article shall be construed to prevent the enforcement of other laws or ordinances which prescribe more restrictive limitations.
(Ord. of 10-15-2002, § 10(54-55))
633:
Enforcement of this article shall be the responsibility of the enforcement authority of the city or its designee.
(Ord. of 10-15-2002, § 11(54-56))
634:
The mayor and council of the city or its designee shall take every reasonable precaution to ensure that alarm messages or signals received by the city or the county's communications department are given appropriate attention and are acted upon with dispatch. Neither the city nor its designee, including the county, shall be liable for any omission or neglect regarding the inspection of the installation or alteration of equipment, transmission of alarm signals, alarm messages, or the relaying of any such signals or messages to the communications department. Further, neither the city nor its designee, including the county, shall be liable for any failure or neglect to respond appropriately upon receipt of a signal from an alarm system, or for the failure or neglect of the communications department or any other person or agency providing dispatch or monitoring services to properly notify any police, fire or other emergency response departments providing services to the city.
(Ord. of 10-15-2002, § 12(54-57))
635:
(a) Any person who owns, leases or occupies property and installs or has installed an alarm system on the premises without obtaining a permit therefor, or alters or has altered an existing alarm system without a permit therefor; or violates any other provision of this article or any regulations promulgated pursuant hereto shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
(b) Any person who intentionally activates any alarm system for any reason other than for those authorized by this article, or during controlled testing of equipment, shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor.
(c) Any person who pleads guilty, is found guilty by the court of violating any provision of this article, or enters a plea of nolo contendere to a citation issued under provisions of this article, may have any business license or occupational tax certificate issued by the city suspended or revoked. Procedures for such suspension or revocation of a business license or occupational tax certificate shall be the same as those set forth in the city occupational license ordinance.
(Ord. of 10-15-2002, § 13(54-58))
636:
Any owner or authorized agent installing or altering an alarm system shall apply to the permitting authority on a form supplied by the permitting authority for a permit to have the alarm system installed or altered on the premises. No such alarm system may be installed or altered after adoption of this section, prior to the issuance of a permit by the permitting authority.
(Ord. of 10-15-2002, § 14(54-59))
637:
The installation and alteration of alarm systems shall be in accordance with article 760, Fire Protective Signaling Systems, of the National Electrical Code, as adopted and amended by the state, and the following NFPA standards, as adopted and amended by the state:
(1) Standard 71, standard for the installation, maintenance, and use of central station signaling systems.
(2) Standard 72-B, standard for the installation, maintenance, and use of auxiliary protective signaling systems for fire alarm service.
(3) Standard 72-C, standard for the installation, maintenance, and use of remote station protective signaling system.
(4) Standard 72-D, standard for the installation, maintenance, and use of remote station protective signaling systems for watchman, fire alarm, and supervisory service.
(5) Standard 72-E, standard on automatic fire detectors.
(6) Standard 74, standard for the installation, maintenance, and use of household fire warning equipment.
(Ord. of 10-15-2002, § 15(54-60))
638:
An owner shall not use or operate, attempt to use or operate, or cause to be used or operated, or arrange, adjust, program or otherwise provide or install any device or combination of devices that will, upon being activated, either mechanically, electronically, or by any other automatic means, call and deliver a recorded message to any telephone number assigned to the city or its designee under this article, including, but not limited to, the county communications department.
(Ord. of 10-15-2002, § 16(54-61))
639:
Except as otherwise authorized by the city or its designee, including the county director of communications, an owner shall not place, install, join, connect or otherwise locate any central station alarm system equipment or device for direct access with the city or the county communications department.
(Ord. of 10-15-2002, § 17(54-62))
640:
The owner of an alarm system shall be responsible for the proper installation and operation of the alarm system and shall obtain a written description of the function of the system along with the procedure and means for activating and deactivating the system.
(Ord. of 10-15-2002, § 18(54-63))
641:
Any owner who shall have in excess of three unauthorized alarms within a 12-month period immediately preceding the last unauthorized alarm shall be deemed in violation of this article and be subject to a user fee of in the amount established by the city and amendable by resolution per each unauthorized alarm in excess of the first three unauthorized alarm occurrences. Any owner who shall have in excess of six unauthorized alarms within a 12-month period immediately preceding the last unauthorized alarm shall be deemed in violation of this article and be subject to a user fee in the amount established by the city and amendable by resolution per unauthorized alarm in excess of six unauthorized alarm occurrences. After nine unauthorized alarms within a 12-month period immediately preceding the last unauthorized alarm, the matter may be referred to the enforcement authority for appropriate action which may include the issuance of a citation and prosecution for violation of this article. Notwithstanding anything contained in this section to the contrary, an owner installing or having installed on the premises a new alarm system (pursuant to a properly issued permit) shall be granted a grace period of 30 days beginning with the date of the new installation during which grace period the user fees provided herein shall not apply.
(Ord. of 10-15-2002, § 19(54-64))
642:
After the occurrence of three unauthorized alarms, as provided in the preceding section, the enforcement authority shall have the right to inspect or cause to be inspected the alarm system at such premises. The enforcement authority may prescribe necessary corrective action resulting from the inspection, and shall give notice to the owner of any such action. A failure to comply with such corrective action within 30 days from the receipt of notice shall be deemed a violation of this article.
(Ord. of 10-15-2002, § 20(54-65))
643:
The owner shall be responsible for deactivating or causing to be deactivated the alarm system within a reasonable time following notification by the enforcement authority or any other city or county department providing notice.
(Ord. of 10-15-2002, § 21(54-66))
645:
The information furnished and secured pursuant to this article is and shall be personal in nature and confidential and not subject to public inspection except to the extent required under provisions of O.C.G.A. title 50, ch. 18, art. 4 (O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71 et seq.). Any employee of the licensing authority, or other person providing the confidential information secured hereunder to any unauthorized person, or using the information to the detriment of the owner, shall be guilty of a violation of this article and subject to the penalties hereunder.
(Ord. of 10-15-2002, § 23(54-68))
646:
The enforcement authority, or other city or the county departments having an interest therein, may from time to time promulgate such rules and regulations as it deems proper concerning the permit, application process, alarm installation and alteration, use and maintenance, testing of alarms, and any other procedures concerning alarm systems.
(Ord. of 10-15-2002, § 24(54-69))
647:
No person shall operate any audible alarm system that does not have an automatic 15-minute shut-off after activation. The enforcement authority shall take all appropriate actions to shut off an audible alarm that does not automatically shut off within 15 minutes of activation.
(Ord. of 10-15-2002, § 25(54-70))
648:
Any person who is of the opinion that a user fee contemplated by this article has been incorrectly assessed may appeal such assessment to the city or its designee, including the director of the department of communications (the director). The appeal shall be in writing and be received by the city or the department of communications within ten days from the receipt of notice of the assessment. Following the receipt of the appeal, the city or director, as applicable, shall schedule a hearing not less than ten days from the receipt of the appeal, and notice thereof shall be provided to all parties having an interest in the disposition of the appeal. In cases where an appeal is made to the director, any decision by the director shall be provided to the parties attending the hearing within ten days of the hearing. If unsatisfied with the decision of the director, the party appealing the assessment may thereafter appeal such decision to the city council.
(Ord. of 10-15-2002, § 26(54-71))
652:
Footnote 1:
State Law reference— Erosion and Sedimentation Act of 1975, O.C.G.A. 12-7-1 et seq.; local ordinances governing land-disturbing activities, O.C.G.A. § 12-7-5.
653:
This article shall be known as the city "Soil Erosion, Sedimentation and Pollution Control Ordinance."
(Ord. No. 2010-04, pt. 2(38-26), xx-xx-2010; Ord. No. 2017-01, § 1(38-1), 1-23-2017)
654:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Best management practices (BMPs) means these include sound conservation and engineering practices to prevent and minimize erosion and resultant sedimentation, which are consistent with, and no less stringent than, those practices contained in the Manual for Erosion and Sediment Control in Georgia published by the commission as of January 1 of the year in which the land-disturbing activity was permitted.
Board means the board of natural resources.
Buffer means the area of land immediately adjacent to the banks of state waters in its natural state of vegetation, which facilitates the protection of water quality and aquatic habitat.
Certified personnel means a person who has successfully completed the appropriate certification course approved by the state soil and water conservation commission.
Coastal marshlands means shall have the same meaning as in O.C.G.A. § 12-5-282.
Commission means the state soil and water conservation commission (GSWCC).
CPESC means certified professional in erosion and sediment control with current certification by EnviroCert, Inc., which is also referred to as CPESC or CPESC, Inc.
Cut means a portion of land surface or area from which earth has been removed or will be removed by excavation; the depth below original ground surface to the excavated surface. Also known as excavation.
Department means the state department of natural resources (DNR).
Design professional means a professional licensed by the state in the field of engineering, architecture, landscape architecture, forestry, geology, or land surveying; or a person that is a certified professional in erosion and sediment control (CPESC) with a current certification by EnviroCert, Inc. Design professionals shall practice in a manner that complies with applicable state law governing professional licensure.
Director means the director of the environmental protection division or an authorized representative.
District means the county soil and water conservation district.
Division means the environmental protection division (EPD) of the state department of natural resources.
Drainage structure means a device composed of a virtually nonerodible material such as concrete, steel, plastic or other such material that conveys water from one place to another by intercepting the flow and carrying it to a release point for stormwater management, drainage control, or flood control purposes.
Erosion means the process by which land surface is worn away by the action of wind, water, ice or gravity.
Erosion, sedimentation and pollution control plan means a plan required by the Erosion and Sedimentation Act of 1975, O.C.G.A. § 12-7-1 et seq., that includes, as minimum protections, at least as stringent as the state general permit, best management practices, and requirements in section 16-22(c).
Fill means a portion of land surface to which soil or other solid material has been added; the depth above the original ground surface or an excavation.
Final stabilization means all soil disturbing activities at the site have been completed, and that for unpaved areas and areas not covered by permanent structures and areas located outside the waste disposal limits of a landfill cell that has been certified by EPD for waste disposal, 100 percent of the soil surface is uniformly covered in permanent vegetation with a density of 70 percent or greater, or landscaped according to the plan (uniformly covered with landscaping materials in planned landscape areas), or equivalent permanent stabilization measures as defined in the manual (excluding a crop of annual vegetation and seeding of target crop perennials appropriate for the region). Final stabilization applies to each phase of construction.
Finished grade means the final elevation and contour of the ground after cutting or filling and conforming to the proposed design.
Grading means altering the shape of ground surfaces to a predetermined condition; this includes stripping, cutting, filling, stockpiling and shaping or any combination thereof and shall include the land in its cut or filled condition.
Ground elevation means the original elevation of the ground surface prior to cutting or filling.
Land-disturbing activity means any activity which may result in soil erosion from water or wind and the movement of sediments into state waters or onto lands within the state, including, but not limited to, clearing, dredging, grading, excavating, transporting, and filling of land but not including agricultural practices as described in section 16-21(5).
Larger common plan of development or sale means a contiguous area where multiple separate and distinct construction activities are occurring under one plan of development or sale. The term "plan" means an announcement; piece of documentation such as a sign, public notice or hearing, sales pitch, advertisement, drawing, permit application, zoning request, or computer design; or physical demarcation such as boundary signs, lot stakes, or surveyor markings, indicating that construction activities may occur on a specific plot.
Local issuing authority means the mayor and council of any county or municipality which is certified pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 12-7-8(a).
Metropolitan River Protection Act (MRPA) means a state law referenced as O.C.G.A. § 12-5-440 et seq. which addresses environmental and developmental matters in certain metropolitan river corridors and their drainage basins.
Natural ground surface means the ground surface in its original state before any grading, excavation or filling.
Nephelometric turbidity units (NTUs) means numerical units of measure based upon photometric analytical techniques for measuring the light scattered by finely divided particles of a substance in suspension. This technique is used to estimate the extent of turbidity in water in which colloidally dispersed or suspended particles are present.
NOI means a notice of intent form provided by EPD for coverage under the state general permit.
NOT means a notice of termination form provided by EPD to terminate coverage under the state general permit.
Operator means the parties that have:
(1) Operational control of construction project plans and specifications, including the ability to make modifications to those plans and specifications; or
(2) Day-to-day operational control of those activities that are necessary to ensure compliance with an erosion, sedimentation and pollution control plan for the site or other permit conditions, such as a person authorized to direct workers at a site to carry out activities required by the erosion, sedimentation and pollution control plan or to comply with other permit conditions.
Outfall means the location where stormwater in a discernible, confined and discrete conveyance, leaves a facility or site or, if there is a receiving water on-site, becomes a point source discharging into that receiving water.
Permit means the authorization necessary to conduct a land-disturbing activity under the provisions of this chapter.
Phase orphased means sub-parts or segments of construction projects where the sub-part or segment is constructed and stabilized prior to completing construction activities on the entire construction site.
Project means the entire proposed development project regardless of the size of the area of land to be disturbed.
Properly designed means designed in accordance with the design requirements and specifications contained in the Manual for Erosion and Sediment Control in Georgia (Manual) published by the state soil and water conservation commission as of January 1 of the year in which the land-disturbing activity was permitted and amendments to the manual as approved by the commission up until the date of NOI submittal.
Roadway drainage structure means a device such as a bridge, culvert, or ditch, composed of a virtually nonerodible material such as concrete, steel, plastic, or other such material that conveys water under a roadway by intercepting the flow on one side of a traveled roadway consisting of one or more defined lanes, with or without shoulder areas, and carrying water to a release point on the other side.
Sediment means solid material, both organic and inorganic, that is in suspension, is being transported, or has been moved from its site of origin by wind, water, ice, or gravity as a product of erosion.
Sedimentation means the process by which eroded material is transported and deposited by the action of water, wind, ice or gravity.
Soil and water conservation district approved plan means an erosion, sedimentation and pollution control plan approved in writing by the county soil and water conservation district.
Stabilization means the process of establishing an enduring soil cover of vegetation by the installation of temporary or permanent structures for the purpose of reducing to a minimum the erosion process and the resultant transport of sediment by wind, water, ice or gravity.
State general permit means the National Pollution Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) general permit or permits for stormwater runoff from construction activities as is now in effect or as may be amended or reissued in the future pursuant to the state's authority to implement the same through federal delegation under the Federal Water Pollution Control Act, 33 USC 1251 et seq., as amended, and O.C.G.A. § 12-5-30(f).
State waters means any and all rivers, streams, creeks, branches, lakes, reservoirs, ponds, drainage systems, springs, wells, and other bodies of surface or subsurface water, natural or artificial, lying within or forming a part of the boundaries of the state which are not entirely confined and retained completely upon the property of a single individual, partnership, or corporation.
Structural erosion, sedimentation and pollution control practices means practices for the stabilization of erodible or sediment-producing areas by utilizing the mechanical properties of matter for the purpose of either changing the surface of the land or storing, regulating or disposing of runoff to prevent excessive sediment loss. Examples of structural erosion and sediment control practices are riprap, sediment basins, dikes, level spreaders, waterways or outlets, diversions, grade stabilization structures and sediment traps, etc. Such practices can be found in the publication Manual for Erosion and Sediment Control in Georgia.
Trout streams means all streams or portions of streams within the watershed as designated by the wildlife resources division of the state department of natural resources under the provisions of the Georgia Water Quality Control Act, O.C.G.A. § 12-5-20 et seq., in the rules and regulations for water quality control, EPD Rule 391-3-6 (Ga. Comp. Rules and Regs. 391-3-6) at www.epd.georgia.gov. Streams designated as primary trout waters are defined as water supporting a self- sustaining population of rainbow, brown or brook trout. Streams designated as secondary trout waters are those in which there is no evidence of natural trout reproduction, but are capable of supporting trout throughout the year. First order trout waters are streams into which no other streams flow except springs.
Vegetative erosion and sedimentation control measures means measures for the stabilization of erodible or sediment-producing areas by covering the soil with means:
(1) Permanent seeding, sprigging or planting, producing long-term vegetative cover:
(2) Temporary seeding, producing short-term vegetative cover; or

Such measures can be found in the publication Manual for Erosion and Sediment Control in Georgia.
Watercourse means any natural or artificial watercourse, stream, river, creek, channel, ditch, canal, conduit, culvert, drain, waterway, gully, ravine, or wash in which water flows either continuously or intermittently and which has a definite channel, bed and banks, and including any area adjacent thereto subject to inundation by reason of overflow or floodwater.
Wetlands means those areas that are inundated or saturated by surface or groundwater at a frequency and duration sufficient to support, and that, under normal circumstances, do support a prevalence of vegetation typically adapted for life in saturated soil conditions. Wetlands generally include swamps, marshes, bogs, and similar areas.
